transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~51 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Jared Lawson (CTO - Arclight), Priya Menon (Lead ML Eng), Samir Gupta (Finance)

Auto-generated summary (short):
- Goal: scope a 4-week POC to validate cost model and perf for Arclight's summarization / extraction workload.
- Success criteria: 95th pctl latency < 350ms for 512-token generations (hosted path) OR throughput 2000 tokens/s on Dedicated, accuracy within 1.5% of baseline.
- Key asks: sample traces, budget envelope, security checklist.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, quick intro - im maya, AE on the account. Ethan from our se team is here to talk perf and cost.
[00:08] Jared Lawson: hey thanks, Jared here. we'll keep it tight, Priya and Samir on the call too.
[00:12] Ethan Cho: hi all, quick agenda - workload sizing, success criteria, benchmarks, then cost model and deployment options. sound good?
[00:18] Priya Menon: yep that works. real quick context: our prod pipeline does document summarization and entity extraction - average input length around 700 tokens, responses avg 150 tokens, about 120k requests per day, peak 2x. accuracy needs to be within 1.5% f1 of our current model.
[00:35] Maya Patel: great. so first question - is the 120k/day the real rough steady state or just projected?
[00:40] Priya Menon: steady plus growth - monthly growth ~8%. during business hours we see 70% of traffic.
[00:46] Ethan Cho: ok good. for cost modeling we usually break it into tokens per month, average tokens per request * requests, plus overhead for system prompts and reranks. with your numbers: (700 in + 150 out) ~ 850 tokens per request * 120k = ~102M tokens/month. does that align with your traces?
[01:08] Priya Menon: yes John's sample trace we shared offline matches that ballpark, we included some long docs too.
[01:13] Jared Lawson: big question - hosted vs dedicated vs private. security's important but also cost.
[01:18] Maya Patel: understood. quick high-level: hosted gives fastest time-to-value and lower operational overhead, per-token unit costs are higher; dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale but requires commit/contract; private (VPC/on-prem) is for strict compliance, higher onboarding time. for the POC we can do hosted or dedicated pilot depending on budget.
[01:32] Samir Gupta: can you give ballpark per-token numbers so we can compare vs our current infra?
[01:37] Ethan Cho: sure - ballparks only during scoping: for a high-quality 34B-ish open model on hosted, inference costs roughly $0.00035 - $0.0006 per generated token depending on batching and caching. embeddings and smaller models cheaper. with quantization and Dedicated we can push down unit to ~$0.00012 - $0.00025 per generated token but that assumes sustained throughput and some model-compat quantization.
[01:58] Priya Menon: those ranges are helpful. how do batching/caching affect latency? we need 95th pctl latency under 350ms ideally.
[02:06] Ethan Cho: important tradeoff - batching increases throughput and lowers cost per token, but can add queuing delay. we typically use small dynamic batches for latency-sensitive routes (target batch sizes of 4-8) to keep p95 below 300-350ms for short responses. for larger requests we rely on prefix/KV caching to avoid re-compute of prompts - if there's repetition in your corpus we can cut compute by 20-60%. note: in transcribed notes you might see 'KV cash' from auto transcript.
[02:34] Jared Lawson: interesting - most of our requests reuse company headers and boilerplate, so prefix caching might help. can you estimate cost reductions?
[02:41] Ethan Cho: yes - with a conservative estimate 25% token reduction from prefix/KV cache across your workload is reasonable; if we detect heavy repetition we can tune caching and reduce tokens 40%+. combined with batching and quantization for dedicated we might hit an effective cost per output token near $0.0001 in optimistic cases.
[03:00] Priya Menon: curious about benchmark setup - what do you need from us to run perf tests?
[03:05] Ethan Cho: we need sample traces (a representative 5k request CSV or ndjson), target SLOs, and a week window for running tests. Redwood will run tests on both hosted and dedicated (if you want a dedicated pilot) - measure latency percentiles, GPU util, tokens/sec, and cost per token. we'll share raw logs + a perf spreadsheet.
[03:25] Maya Patel: also we'll include a model variant matrix - quant levels, model sizes (13B, 34B), and expected quality tradeoffs.
[03:32] Samir Gupta: about budget - we can allocate an initial POC budget of $30k. is that enough?
[03:37] Ethan Cho: yes that's workable for a 4-week POC focusing on hosted + one dedicated pilot node for spot checks. with your token volume 102M tokens/month, hosted at $0.0004/token is about $40k/month, but the POC can be scoped smaller - run a controlled 5k request benchmark set and extrapolate. Dedicated pilot amortizes differently - we'd propose a short reserved node to validate throughput.
[03:59] Priya Menon: accuracy/regression checks - will Redwood run evals against our golden set?
[04:03] Maya Patel: yes we'll run automated evals and diffed outputs to track quality regressions, and tie alerts to any >1% drop in F1. we'll include outputs in the benchmark report.
[04:14] Jared Lawson: security - we need SOC2, SSO, audit logs, KMS integration and VPC peering for Private later. how mature are these?
[04:22] Maya Patel: we are SOC2 certified, have SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS support for Dedicated/Private. for hosted we provide managed encryption at rest and transit; for customer-managed keys we use our Private option with KMS/HSM integrations. we'll send the security pack after the call.
[04:36] Samir Gupta: how about data retention and logs? we prefer logs for audits but only limited retention.
[04:41] Ethan Cho: we can configure retention windows and log redaction; audit logs for admin actions are standard in Redwood Console. we'll include details in the security doc.
[04:51] Priya Menon: timeline - if we get the sample traces tomorrow can you start the benchmark next week?
[04:56] Ethan Cho: yes. proposed timeline:
- by 2026-05-21: Arclight provides sample traces, golden set, and SLOs.
- 2026-05-22: Redwood sends POC pricing & model/quant profiles.
- week of 2026-05-25: run benchmark (3 day window) and gather perf + quality metrics.
- 2026-05-29: follow-up meeting to review results and discuss Dedicated pilot/contract.
[05:19] Jared Lawson: sounds good. one more question - are there any hidden costs we should prepare for? e.g., storage for cache, network egress?
[05:25] Maya Patel: good callout - network egress and storage for cached keys are usually small relative to compute but we'll list them. also engineering integration time for Private/Dedicated can add upfront onboarding costs. Samir you might want to include a small buffer in the budget.
[05:38] Samir Gupta: will do.
[05:41] Priya Menon: can you sktech an example cost calc for our numbers?
[05:44] Ethan Cho: sure quick calc (rough):
- tokens/month: ~102M tokens.
- Hosted baseline per-output-token: $0.00045 -> ~ $45,900/month.
- With prefix caching 25% reduction -> effective tokens 76.5M -> cost ~$34,425/month.
- With batching/optim and a dedicated pilot quant profile -> per-token ~$0.00018 -> cost ~$13,770/month (plus reserved node fee).
Notes: these numbers exclude a small amount for logging/egress and any SLA premium. We'll provide a detailed spreadsheet.
[06:20] Maya Patel: we'll attach that calc in the pricing spreadsheet.
[06:23] Ethan Cho: also, for latency - to hit p95 <350ms for your 150-token outputs we recommend dynamic batching with max batch 8 and a target service thread latency budget. we'll validate in the benchmark.
[06:36] Jared Lawson: ok great. are there any blockers we should flag now?
[06:39] Priya Menon: internal security review might take a week but not a blocker for the benchmark.
[06:44] Samir Gupta: finance will want a clear ROI case if we move to Dedicated.
[06:48] Maya Patel: understood. we'll include an ROI slide in the follow-up with payback estimates for Dedicated based on your volume.
[06:55] Ethan Cho: last technical note - if you plan to use on-prem/private later, some model variants need different quantization flows, we'll document that. also watch for tokenization differences vs your current model - small delta in token counts can change cost.
[07:10] Jared Lawson: good point.
[07:12] Maya Patel: recap of next steps (quick): Maya will send POC pricing spreadsheet + model/quant profiles by 5/22; Ethan will schedule and run benchmark week of 5/25 and deliver perf + quality report; Priya will send sample workload and golden set by 5/21; Samir to confirm budget by 5/25; schedule follow-up 5/29.
[07:34] Priya Menon: thanks all, appreciate the clear plan.
[07:37] Maya Patel: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links to the security pack and the benchmarks doc.
[07:42] Jared Lawson: thanks everyone bye.
